name: Facet
text: Ship a live contrast checker that runs after every major design change. It flags low-contrast elements in real time, so designers see violations immediately—not after a merge or a user complaint. The trade-off is a small performance hit during active design tweaks, but it prevents costly fixes later and keeps the interface accessible by default.

name: Pane
text: The live contrast checker trains designers to ignore warnings like seatbelt chimes—if every tweak spams alerts, they’ll mute the tool or dismiss violations as noise. Instead, ship a pre-commit hook that blocks merges with low-contrast elements, forcing fixes before they reach users; the trade-off is slower iteration for designers, but it guarantees no bad contrast ships. Settle it with a 2-week trial: measure designer complaints vs. post-merge contrast fixes in production.
